clue.text: Meeting prisoner about to breach boundary

parts.note: a convict, a con, is a prisoner

indicators.note: to breach is to break through, so one piece goes into the middle of another

parts.note: a fence marks a boundary
re is Latin-derived for about, concerning

explanation.surface: A jailbird slips past the perimeter for a rendezvous.
explanation.definitionFit: A conference is a formal meeting for discussion.

clue.text: Animals in shed with raised temperature

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means moved higher up the word

parts.note: cast means shed, as a snake casts its skin

explanation.surface: Animals in an outhouse running a fever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' looks like a building; it is the verb CAST. 'raised' moves its T up a place.
explanation.definitionFit: Cats are animals, the familiar domestic pets.

clue.text: An upcoming surgeon, after one year, shows inexperience

indicators.note: after puts the surgeon behind the one
upcoming in a down clue means read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a vet is an animal surgeon

explanation.surface: A trainee surgeon, a year in, still shows his greenness.
explanation.definitionFit: Naivety is innocence, lack of worldly experience or judgement.

clue.text: Full of initiative, come on stage with pressure mounting

parts.note: enter is the stage direction to come on
rising means mounting, increasing

explanation.surface: A go-getting actor walks on as the tension builds.
explanation.definitionFit: Enterprising people are resourceful, keen to start new ventures.

clue.text: Recruited eldest in cooking

indicators.note: cooking as in cooking the books means fiddling, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The oldest child was drafted into kitchen duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Enlisted means signed up for the armed forces, enrolled.

clue.text: Kind of yellow grass

definitions.meaning: ... yellow is a bright shade named after the songbird
a grass is British slang for an informer, and so is a ..., one who sings to police

explanation.definitionFit: Canary is a shade of yellow and slang for an informer who sings to police.

clue.text: Something milky-white obtained from coco-palm

indicators.note: obtained from says the letters are taken straight out of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Milky stuff extracted from a coconut palm, as coconut milk would be.
explanation.definitionFit: The opal is a gemstone typically milky-white with flashes of colour.

clue.text: Promises plasma's first over fifty inches

indicators.note: over in a down clue means placed above, so it comes earlier
first takes the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
edges is a verb meaning inches, moves slowly

explanation.surface: An advert boasting a plasma screen over fifty inches wide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inches' looks like screen size; it is the verb EDGES.
explanation.definitionFit: Pledges are solemn promises or undertakings.

clue.text: Fancied grabbing short time with editor, having similar outlook

indicators.note: grabbing means seizing hold, so it closes around another piece

parts.note: liked means fancied
min is short for minute, a short time

explanation.surface: Someone attracted to a quick spell with the editor because they think alike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short time' is a minute cut short, the usual crossword MIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Like-minded people share the same views and tastes.

clue.text: Somehow train sloth for races

indicators.note: somehow says the letters are got into shape in some unstated way, an arrangement signal

explanation.surface: An absurd plan to coach a sloth for athletic contests.
explanation.definitionFit: Triathlons are endurance races combining swimming, cycling and running.

clue.text: Queen goes between bishop and king, idiot!

indicators.note: goes between places one piece in the gap between two others

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
K is the chess abbreviation for king
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword queen

explanation.surface: A chess player moves the queen between bishop and king and is called a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: BERK is British slang for a stupid person.
explanation.definitionFit: Berk is a mild British insult meaning a fool or dimwit.

clue.text: Cutter in fleet Yanks repaired

indicators.note: repaired means fixed up, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A cutter, a small boat, in the American fleet fixed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutter' looks like a naval boat; it is a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stanley knife is a retractable-blade utility knife, a cutting tool.

clue.text: Clobber good listener

parts.note: an ear is the organ that listens

explanation.surface: Hit a good listener, as an odd command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clobber' looks like a verb, but here it is British slang for clothes and kit.
explanation.definitionFit: Clobber is informal British for gear: clothes and equipment.

clue.text: Manoeuvre layers of rock and stone

parts.note: strata are layers of rock
a gem is a precious stone

explanation.surface: A geologist's inventory of rock beds and stones, with a verb tacked on front.
explanation.definitionFit: A stratagem is a cunning plan or manoeuvre to outwit someone.

clue.text: Destroy article covered in oil, better to be replaced

indicators.note: covered in means wrapped by, with the article enclosed
to be replaced means put back differently, so the letters change position

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An instruction to wipe out an oily article and replace it with a better one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be replaced' mixes the nine letters into OBLITERTE before 'covered in' wraps them around the article.
explanation.definitionFit: To obliterate is to wipe out completely, demolish.

clue.text: Best year to relocate plants

indicators.note: to relocate is to move things around, so these letters take new places

explanation.surface: Gardening advice on the ideal year to move your plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Bay trees are evergreen laurels, shrubs grown in gardens and pots.

clue.text: Total agreement part of run is onerous

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Everyone agrees that running is a chore.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in unison means in complete accord, everyone together.

clue.text: Training on little part for tool

parts.note: drill is training, as in military drill
a bit is a small part

explanation.surface: Instruction in a minor component of a tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A drill bit is a tool fitted to a drill to bore holes.

clue.text: Unwelcomely occupy island home with fine interior

indicators.note: interior says the following piece sits inside the home

parts.note: a nest is a bird's home
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: Squatters take over an island house with a lovely interior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with fine interior' puts F inside NEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Pests infest a place, swarming over it in unwanted numbers.

clue.text: Make way

definitions.meaning: to make, shape or form something
a way, as in a manner or mode of doing something

explanation.definitionFit: Fashion means to shape something, and also a manner of doing it.

clue.text: Regrets delving into work, this writer's terrible

indicators.note: delving into means going inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: to go is to work, as in a machine that goes
rues means regrets
this writer is the setter, me; the 's is read as is

explanation.surface: A writer confesses their regrets about their work are awful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' here is GO, as when a machine goes; 'this writer' is the setter, giving ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Gruesome means horrible or ghastly, causing revulsion.

clue.text: Scrap noted thrown around vacant dorm

indicators.note: around means surrounding the next piece
thrown means flung about, so the letters are mixed up
vacant means empty, leaving only the outside letters

explanation.surface: A note about bits of rubbish thrown around an empty dormitory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown' mixes the five letters into ODENT, split around the dorm's shell by 'around'.
explanation.definitionFit: An oddment is a leftover scrap or fragment.

clue.text: Girl served up popular fizzy drink

indicators.note: served up in a down clue means placed upwards, read from bottom

parts.note: in means popular, fashionable
cola is a fizzy soft drink

explanation.surface: A girl was given a popular soft drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicola is a girl's first name.

clue.text: Directed to enter crackers aisle for must-have item

indicators.note: to enter means to go inside, placing one piece within another
crackers means crazy, so the letters of the word beside it go mad

parts.note: sent means directed, dispatched

explanation.surface: Shoppers are sent down the biscuit aisle for a staple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crackers' looks like the biscuits in the aisle, but it shuffles the word to ESIAL, which 'to enter' then opens.
explanation.definitionFit: An essential is something indispensable, a necessity you cannot do without.

clue.text: Pirate's fourth child?

parts.note: a kid is a child
D is the fourth letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A buccaneer's fourth offspring.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'. Captain William Kidd was a notorious 17th-century pirate.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Kidd is one of history's most famous pirates, hanged in 1701.

clue.text: Exhausted American feds abandoning borders

indicators.note: abandoning borders means losing outer letters, leaving the middle

explanation.surface: Tired US federal agents leave the border patrol.
explanation.definitionFit: Used, as in used up, means spent or exhausted.

clue.text: Maybe Cameron's leader dismissed as mad

indicators.note: leader dismissed means the first letter is sacked

parts.note: David Cameron is a former UK prime minister, so his first name is one example

explanation.surface: A political story about a party leader sacked for being crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cameron's leader' tempts as C; 'Maybe Cameron's' gives his first name DAVID, whose leader goes.
explanation.definitionFit: To be mad about something is to be avid, keenly enthusiastic for it.

clue.text: Instability of boss drunk with wine hugging empty barrel

indicators.note: hugging means holding something close, wrapped around it
drunk means tipsy, so the letters of the words beside it reel about
empty means a word stripped of its contents, leaving only the outside

explanation.surface: A drunken boss sways, clutching an empty wine barrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' mixes the eight letters into WOBINESS; 'hugging' has them wrap the empty barrel's two outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Wobbliness is unsteadiness, a tendency to totter.

clue.text: Flier reprinted regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, taking every other letter

explanation.surface: A leaflet that keeps being reprinted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flier' looks like a printed leaflet; it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The erne is a sea eagle, a big bird and crossword regular.

clue.text: Abused whiskey and wine, consumed inside

parts.note: malt is a type of whisky

indicators.note: inside places the eaten piece within the wine

parts.note: red is wine by its colour
ate means consumed

explanation.surface: Someone misused whiskey and wine, swallowing them down.
explanation.walkthrough: Wine by colour is a crossword staple: RED, ROSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To maltreat is to treat cruelly, so abused and maltreated are synonyms.
